chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba al-Hashimi, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan, meaning Musa (peace be upon him), about the man who copulates with his wife during the journey while it is the month of Ramadan. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does sexual intercourse with one's wife during Ramadan invalidate the fast?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi, narrated by Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), clarifies that sexual intercourse with one's wife during Ramadan while traveling does not break the fast, distinguishing it from the ruling during stationary residence. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it highlights the concession (rukhsah) granted to travelers, contrasting with the general consensus that intercourse invalidates the fast when not traveling. The phrase 'la ba'sa bihi' indicates permissibility without nullification, reflecting the practical ease Islam affords to those on journeys.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdul Malik Bin Utba Al Hashimy who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Musa<sup>asws</sup>, about the man who copulates with his wife during the journey and it is during a Month of Ramazan. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Utbah al-Hashimiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who experiences sexual relation with his wife during a journey in the month of Ramadan. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
